issues.legal_issue: A suit alleging breach of a public religious trust and seeking to compel a trustee to perform duties for the trust’s objects falls within the special trust-suit procedure when its relief is akin to the specified administration reliefs, even if framed as an injunction.
material_facts: The suit was brought in a representative capacity concerning a public religious trust.
The plaint alleged that the trustee was not using the religious institution for its dedicated purposes and was obstructing public access and religious recitations.
The plaintiffs sought an injunction to prevent interference and to compel performance of the trustee’s duties, rather than expressly seeking one of the enumerated forms of relief.
The plaintiffs had not obtained the required written consent before instituting the suit.
issues.conclusion: The suit was in substance one for relief under section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure and was not maintainable because it was not instituted in conformity with that section.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 92(1) and (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a suit concerning a public charitable or religious trust, founded on an alleged breach of trust or requiring court directions for its administration, must seek one or more of the specified forms of relief and be instituted in the prescribed manner. The residual relief provision covers relief akin to the specified administration reliefs, not relief of a wholly different nature. The suit’s nature is determined from the plaint, not the written statement. The Court relied on Abdur Rahim v. Syed Abu Mahomed Barkat Ali Shah for the construction of the residual clause; Mahant Pragdasji Guru Bhagwandasji v. Patel Ishwarlalbhai Narsibhai and Swami Paramatmanand Saraswati v. Ramji Tripathi for the requirements and scope of such a suit; and distinguished Ganpat Pujari v. Kanaiyalal Marwari and Harendra Nath Bhattacharya v. Kalimaram Das.

rule.if: trust_administration_proceeding and public_religious_or_charitable_trust and (trust_breach_alleged or court_directions_needed) and trustee_duty_enforcement_sought and relief_akin_to_administration_reliefs and not required_filing_procedure_followed

predicates.trust_administration_proceeding: The proceeding seeks court relief concerning the administration of a trust.
predicates.public_religious_or_charitable_trust: The trust involved is for a public religious or charitable purpose.
predicates.trust_breach_alleged: The claimants allege that a trustee has breached duties owed to the trust.
predicates.court_directions_needed: The claimants seek directions from the court for the trust’s administration.
predicates.trustee_duty_enforcement_sought: The claimants seek to compel a trustee to perform duties in furtherance of the trust’s objects.
predicates.relief_akin_to_administration_reliefs: The relief sought is akin in nature to relief concerning the administration of the trust.
predicates.required_filing_procedure_followed: The claimants instituted the proceeding in the required manner.

issues.definition: When a trust-administration proceeding concerns a public religious or charitable trust, alleges breach or need for court directions, seeks enforcement of trustee duties through akin administrative relief, and does not follow the required filing procedure, the suit is not maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: The death of one plaintiff does not cause an appeal to abate when the suit was brought in a representative capacity for the general public.
material_facts: The suit was brought by plaintiffs in a representative capacity on behalf of devotees of the religious institution.
One plaintiff died while the second appeal was pending, and no legal representative was substituted for that plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The death of one plaintiff did not cause the appeal to abate.
issues.legal_principle: A suit prosecuted in a representative capacity for the general public is not a suit prosecuted by individuals for their own interests, and the death of one plaintiff does not make the appeal incompetent. The Court followed Raja Anand Rao v. Ramdas Daduram.

predicates.representative_public_proceeding: The proceeding is brought by claimants in a representative capacity for the general public.
predicates.representative_dies_during_appeal: One of the representatives dies while the appeal is pending.

issues.definition: When a representative in a proceeding for the general public dies during the appeal, the appeal does not abate.
